# Delivery & Logistics Policy
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Delivery Windows
1.1 Standard priority orders must arrive within the quoted lead time plus a
2-day grace period. High priority orders have a 1-day grace period. Urgent
priority orders have zero grace period — any delay is recorded immediately.

Section 2: Delay Classification
2.1 Delays are classified by severity:
   - Minor Delay: 1–3 days past the grace period.
   - Moderate Delay: 4–7 days past the grace period.
   - Severe Delay: more than 7 days past the grace period.

2.2 A Severe Delay on an Urgent priority order automatically triggers a
notification to the Supply Chain Risk team and a note on the supplier's
profile.

Section 3: Seasonal Adjustments
3.1 During the November–January peak season, expected delivery windows may
be extended by mutual agreement, but the Supplier must confirm any adjusted
date in writing at least 5 business days before the original due date.

3.2 Failure to proactively communicate seasonal delays is treated as a
standard late delivery under the Late Delivery Penalties in the Master
Supplier Agreement.

Section 4: Carrier and Routing
4.1 Suppliers are responsible for selecting a carrier capable of meeting the
agreed delivery window. Repeated delays attributed to carrier choice do not
exempt the Supplier from late delivery penalties.

Section 5: Proof of Delivery
5.1 Suppliers must provide proof of delivery (tracking confirmation or signed
receipt) within 24 hours of delivery for all orders above $5,000 in value.

# Inventory Management Policy
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Reorder Point Methodology
1.1 Every product has a defined Reorder Level, calculated as approximately
15–35% of average monthly demand, adjusted for the supplier's average lead
time and demand variability.

1.2 When current stock falls below the Reorder Level, the product is flagged
as "Low Stock" and a replenishment purchase order should be initiated within
2 business days.

Section 2: Minimum Inventory Levels
2.1 The Company's minimum acceptable inventory level for any active product is
the Reorder Level itself. Stock is not permitted to be allowed to reach zero
for products with active monthly demand, except for discontinued items.

2.2 Products flagged Low Stock for more than 10 consecutive business days
without a corresponding purchase order must be escalated to the Inventory
Manager.

Section 3: Safety Stock for Critical Categories
3.1 Products in the "Electronics" and "Machinery Parts" categories, which
have longer average lead times, should maintain a safety stock buffer of an
additional 10% above the standard Reorder Level.

Section 4: Excess Inventory
4.1 Inventory exceeding 4x the Reorder Level for more than 60 days is
classified as Excess Inventory and reviewed for potential overstock write-down
or demand forecast correction.

Section 5: Cycle Counting
5.1 High-value products (unit cost above $200) are cycle-counted monthly.
All other products are cycle-counted quarterly.

Section 6: Inventory Valuation
6.1 Inventory value is calculated as current stock multiplied by unit cost,
and is reported at the category level in the Executive Dashboard.

# Procurement Policy
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Purpose
This policy establishes the rules for how the Company sources, evaluates, and
purchases goods and services from external suppliers.

Section 2: Supplier Onboarding
2.1 New suppliers must complete a Supplier Registration Form and pass an initial
risk assessment before being added to the Approved Supplier List.

2.2 Suppliers handling categories classified as "Critical" (Electronics,
Machinery Parts) require a facility audit before approval.

Section 3: Purchase Order Authorization Limits
3.1 Purchase orders under $10,000 may be approved by a Procurement Analyst.

3.2 Purchase orders between $10,000 and $100,000 require approval from a
Procurement Manager.

3.3 Purchase orders above $100,000 require approval from the Director of
Procurement and Finance sign-off.

Section 4: Competitive Bidding
4.1 Any new sourcing arrangement expected to exceed $50,000 in annual spend must
go through a competitive bidding process with at least three quotes.

4.2 Sole-sourcing (using a single supplier without competitive bids) is only
permitted for proprietary components with no viable alternative supplier, and
must be documented with a Sole Source Justification form.

Section 5: Supplier Diversification
5.1 To reduce concentration risk, no single supplier should account for more
than 40% of total spend within a product category, where alternative suppliers
exist.

5.2 Categories with fewer than 2 active approved suppliers are flagged as
"Single Point of Failure" categories and prioritized for supplier diversification
efforts.

Section 6: Cost Review
6.1 Supplier pricing (reflected in the cost index) is reviewed semi-annually.
A cost index more than 20% above the category average requires justification
or renegotiation.

Section 7: Emergency Procurement
7.1 In the event of a supply disruption affecting production, Emergency
Procurement procedures allow expedited approval (single manager sign-off,
regardless of order value) for a maximum of 15 days, after which normal
approval limits resume.

# Purchase Order Guidelines
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Required Fields
1.1 Every purchase order must include: supplier ID, product ID(s), quantity,
unit cost, requested delivery date, priority level, and the responsible
procurement analyst's name.

Section 2: Priority Levels
2.1 Orders may be marked Standard, High, or Urgent.
   - Standard: routine replenishment, standard lead time applies.
   - High: expedited handling requested; supplier should prioritize picking
     and shipping, 1-day grace period on delivery.
   - Urgent: production-critical shortage; zero grace period, and the
     supplier must confirm receipt of the order within 4 business hours.

Section 2: Minimum Order Quantities
2.2 Orders below a supplier's stated Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) may be
consolidated with other pending orders to the same supplier where possible,
to avoid MOQ surcharges.

Section 3: Amendments and Cancellations
3.1 A purchase order may be amended (quantity or delivery date) up to 48 hours
after issuance without penalty, provided the supplier has not yet begun
fulfillment.

3.2 Cancellations after the supplier has begun fulfillment may incur a
cancellation fee of up to 15% of order value, subject to negotiation.

Section 4: Order Matching and Receiving
4.1 Upon receipt, goods are matched against the purchase order (quantity,
product ID, and quality spec) before being logged into inventory. Discrepancies
must be reported within 48 hours of receipt.

Section 5: Record Retention
5.1 Purchase orders and associated delivery records must be retained for a
minimum of 3 years for audit purposes.

# Master Supplier Agreement (Template)
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Scope of Agreement
This agreement governs the supply of goods between SupplySense Manufacturing Group
("the Company") and any registered supplier ("the Supplier"). It applies to all
purchase orders issued under the Company's procurement system.

Section 2: Delivery Obligations
2.1 The Supplier shall deliver goods within the lead time specified on each purchase
order. The standard acceptable delivery window is the quoted lead time plus a
grace period of 2 calendar days.

2.2 A delivery is considered "late" if goods arrive more than 2 days after the
agreed delivery date stated on the purchase order.

2.3 The Supplier must notify the Company's procurement team at least 3 business
days in advance of any anticipated delay.

Section 3: Late Delivery Penalties
3.1 For each late delivery, a penalty of 0.5% of the order value shall be applied
per day of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the total order value.

3.2 If a Supplier records more than 15% of orders as delayed within a rolling
90-day period, the Supplier shall automatically be flagged for a **Performance
Review** (see Section 4).

3.3 Repeated late delivery — defined as three or more late deliveries within any
rolling 60-day window — may result in suspension o

Section 4: Performance Review
4.1 A Performance Review is triggered when a Supplier's on-time delivery rate
falls below 85% over a rolling quarter, or when flagged under Section 3.2.

4.2 The review evaluates: on-time delivery rate, quality score, responsiveness
to communication, and root cause of delays.

Section 5: Quality Requirements
5.1 All goods must meet the quality specifications stated in the applicable
Purchase Order and pass incoming inspection.

5.2 A defect rate above 5% in any shipment gives the Company the right to
reject the shipment in full and request replacement at the Supplier's cost.

Section 6: Termination
6.1 Either party may terminate this agreement with 60 days' written notice.

6.2 The Company may terminate immediately, without notice, in cases of fraud,
repeated safety violations, or breach of confidentiality obligations.

Section 7: Confidentiality
7.1 Both parties agree to keep pricing, forecasts, and proprietary specifications
confidential and not disclose them to third parties without written consent.

# Supplier Evaluation Guidelines
**SupplySense Manufacturing Group — Fictional Document for Demonstration Purposes**

Section 1: Purpose
These guidelines define how supplier performance is scored and how frequently
suppliers must be evaluated.

Section 2: Evaluation Frequency
2.1 All active suppliers are formally evaluated quarterly.

2.2 Suppliers under an active Performance Review (see Master Supplier
Agreement, Section 4) are evaluated monthly until performance is restored
above the review threshold.

Section 3: Scoring Dimensions
3.1 Supplier evaluation considers four weighted dimensions:
   - On-Time Delivery Rate — 40% weight
   - Quality Score — 30% weight
   - Cost Competitiveness (relative to category average) — 20% weight
   - Responsiveness / Communication — 10% weight

Section 4: Risk Classification Requirements
4.1 A supplier is classified as HIGH risk when on-time delivery falls below
70% AND at least one additional dimension (quality or cost) is also below
the acceptable threshold in the same evaluation period.

4.2 A supplier is classified as MEDIUM risk when on-time delivery is between
70–90%, or when a single dimension is significantly underperforming while
others remain acceptable.

Section 5: Minimum Requirements to Remain an Approved Supplier
5.1 Suppliers must maintain a minimum quality score of 70 and an on-time
delivery rate of at least 60% to remain on the Approved Supplier List without
a corrective action plan.

5.2 Any supplier falling below these minimums for two consecutive quarters is
automatically escalated for contract review and potential removal from the
Approved Supplier List.
